ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (Public Act 2009 No 35) ss 15, 22, 23, 24; Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105) ss 189, 201; Companies (Director, Shareholder and Ultimate Holding Company) Information Regulations 2017; Companies Office AML/CFT Guidelines on Customer Due Diligence (2023); Financial Markets Authority AML/CFT Guidelines for Reporting Entities (2023).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled copy of each beneficial owner's passport valid for at least 6 months beyond the date of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority of the beneficial owner's country of citizenship; notarized by a licensed notary in that country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization at the New Zealand Embassy or Consulate if the issuing country is not a Hague Apostille Convention signatory)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled proof of residential address for each director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner (uny 3-month-old utility bill or official bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or bank in the country of residence; notarized by a licensed notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization at the New Zealand Embassy or Consulate if the issuing country is not a Hague Apostille Convention signatory)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or equivalent certificate of legal existence) for any corporate shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner that is a legal entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The corporate registry of the country in which the corporate shareholder or beneficial owner is incorporated
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization at the New Zealand Embassy or Consulate if the issuing country is not a Hague Apostille Convention signatory)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the constitutional documents (Memorandum and Articles of Association, or equivalent) for each corporate entity in the ownership chain above the proposed New Zealand company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The company secretary of the corporate entity and notarized by a licensed notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization at the New Zealand Embassy or Consulate if the issuing country is not a Hague Apostille Convention signatory)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, secretaries, and intended authorized signatories against: (a) the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit (NZ-FIU) Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) list; (b) the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade Sanctions Register under the United Nations Act 1946 and the Russia Sanctions Act 2022; (c) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (d) the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List; and (e) the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) call-for-action listings. Screening must be completed within 24 hours prior to filing incorporation. Any positive match must be escalated to an enhanced due diligence process pursuant to AML/CFT Act 2009 ss 22-24, and the incorporation may not proceed without explicit approval from the designated compliance officer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Name Reservation and Registration online service (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz/companies/register/name-reservation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Latin script (A-Z) and may include Māori words and Latin diacritical marks (macrons). Non-Latin script names (e.g., CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic) are not accepted; a Latin-character transliteration must be submitted. The name must begin with a letter or number; allowed punctuation includes spaces, ampersand, plus sign, comma, period, hyphen, and apostrophe. Maximum length is 100 characters. Any name not in English or Māori must be accompanied by an English translation for the Registrar's distinctiveness and compliance assessment under Companies Act 1993 s 20.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name reservation is rejected, the applicant may request an administrative review from the Companies Office within 20 working days of the refusal using the online 'Request a Name Review' service. The review will be conducted by a senior registrar not involved in the initial decision. If the review upholds the rejection, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of New Zealand on a point of law under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972. Extensions of an approved name reservation are permitted by filing a further 'Application for Reservation of Proposed Company Name' and paying the current fee, which grants an additional 20 working days from the date of extension.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only when it consists of a physical street address maintained by a licensed registered agent and not a PO Box or non-physical virtual location. This satisfies the Companies Act 1993 s 189 requirement for a registered office in New Zealand. For the commercial inspection/testing agency industry, a virtual office is acceptable if the company does not carry on physical inspection services within New Zealand. However, if the company establishes a physical presence, it must register a place of business. Virtual offices that do not support service of process or access to company records will be deemed non-compliant by the NZ Companies Office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated <5% probability within the first 12 months post-incorporation). Probability increases to 20% if on-site inspection operations are established in New Zealand or if an AML/CFT trigger event occurs, such as a reportable suspicious transaction or a change in UBO requiring enhanced scrutiny.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name reservation fee (New Zealand dollar statutory fee converted)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Companies Act 1993 and Companies (Fees) Regulations 2005; current fee 20 working days into the budget.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company incorporation filing fee (standard online application fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Companies Act 1993 and Companies (Fees) Regulations 2005; NZ$150 estimated at USD 0.60.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and registered agent service for first year (physical street address, mail forwarding, regulatory correspondence handling)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed New Zealand Registered Agent (private service provider)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for low-risk non-resident companies; quoted as annual fee, no statutory tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO due diligence, PEP and sanctions screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent compliance consultant or law firm retained for the pre-incorporation due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per hour/engagement; covers OFAC/UN/MFAT/NZ-FIU database checks and report generation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille authentication of the mandatory documentation bundle (4 underlying documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public and the Competent Apostille Authority (e.g., designated government office in the country of origin)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory apostille fees plus market notarial fees; estimated USD 100 per document for four documents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation and mailing of the full incorporation filing package to the New Zealand registered agent, including certified translations if applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for document courier, translation, and courier handling; no statutory tariff.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss. 10 (incorporation by registration), 12 (application for registration), 13 (registration of company), 15 (constitution), 122 (director requirements), 128 (shares and minimum subscription), 161 (registered office), 175 (appointment of officers); Financial Reporting Act 2013 (applicable reporting obligations); Companies (Fees) Regulations 2016 (filing fees).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO), a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZ/CO/01 – Application for Registration of a Company (Incorporation Application) lodged via the New Zealand Companies Office online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under the Companies Act 1993; the company may issue one or more shares with nil or nominal par value as determined by the board. No escrow account rule applies for standard commercial inspection and testing companies, provided the directors meet the 'no-liability' solvency certification requirements under section 13(3).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED / [COMPANY NAME] COMPANY NUMBER [NZBN]: RESOLVED that the share capital in the sum of NZD 1.00 (one New Zealand dollar, or such lesser amount as recorded in the inaugural register) be duly subscribed by the initial member and allotted for nil or nominal consideration as recorded in the share register; RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established and maintained at [Physical Address, City, New Zealand], and that the address for service be recorded with the New Zealand Companies Office and the New Zealand Business Number register; RESOLVED that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as director and chairperson, [Name] be appointed as director, and [Name] be appointed as chief executive officer, company secretary, and compliance officer, each holding office subject to the Companies Act 1993 and the constitution (if adopted); RESOLVED that the board adopts the Company's constitution, if any, and authorizes the opening of corporate bank accounts with an NZ-registered trading bank, the engagement of a New Zealand-registered auditor or chartered accountant, and the execution of any necessary statutory filings and business registrations including the IRD number application and GST registration; RESOLVED that the directors certify solvency in accordance with section 13(3) of the Companies Act 1993 and that the first board meeting be deemed duly constituted and held at the registered office on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Entity Name Reservation and NZBN Pre-registration Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE – online company name availability search and NZBN registry portal (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the New Zealand Companies Office register ensuring the proposed name '[COMPANY NAME] LIMITED' is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered company, foreign company, or reserved name under the Companies Act 1993 s. 22. Submit a name reservation via the online portal if a hold is required, and record the proposed NZBN allocation. The name must comply with the Companies Act 1993 s. 23 (no misleading, offensive, or restricted-name terms including references to 'audit' or 'trust' unless separately licensed).
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and name availability search result
Director consent and identity verification (passport or national ID)
Certificate of incorporation intention / name reservation receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or set aside, file a fresh application with a new distinctive name or file a formal objection/request for administrative review with the Registrar of Companies under section 22(4); otherwise proceed with the registry's recommended alternative name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Incorporation Application and Governing Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE (online lodgement); notarial services by New Zealand Notary Public or Justice of the Peace for certified vero documents where required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Form NZ/CO/01 together with the company constitution (whether in prescribed form or bespoke). Procure notarized or certified copies of the directors' and shareholders' passports, proof of residential address, and director consent forms. Ensure the company has at least one director who resides in New Zealand or is an Australian resident ordinarily resident in Australia and director with an actual New Zealand address (in the case of a sole director resident overseas, appoint a New Zealand-resident director). Verify share structure, restriction provisions of ISIC 7120, and the liability clause. Obtain wet-ink or digital signatures from all incorporators and directors, with witness details as prescribed by the Companies Act 1993 s. 14.
required_dossiers: Consents to appointment of directors (Form NZ/CO/02)
Notarized passports of directors and shareholders
Proof of residential address for directors and shareholders
Solvency certificate in accordance with s. 13(3)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the identity evidence or statutory declarations, resubmit corrected notarized documents and provide supplementary explanations within 5 business days; request an extension of filing deadline via the Companies Office service chat or statutory query resolution process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgement of Incorporation Application and Registration Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE – online incorporation application system (RealMe login or NZBN login).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in via RealMe, complete the company incorporation wizard, confirm the registered office (must be physical address in New Zealand, not a PO Box unless accompanied by a physical service address), enter the NZBN registration data, and select the ISIC/ANZSIC industry classification code corresponding to 'Testing and Analysis Services (ANZSIC 7120)' – commercial inspection and testing. Make payment of the NZD 140.00 filing fee (approximately USD 88.00) through the electronic payment gateway. Upon acceptance, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and allocates the NZBN; the company comes into existence on the date and time of registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or placed in abeyance, review the Registrar's return, cure the listed defects (e.g., invalid registered office or director shortfall), and re-lodge the application within 10 business days; appealable by way of judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register of Directors, Shareholders, and Ultimate Beneficial Ownership Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE – Companies Register and Registrar's compliance unit.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the first 20 working days after incorporation, lodge particulars of directors and any ultimate beneficial owner details, enter all share allotments in the Register of Members, and file an Annual Return confirmation. Maintain a register of ultimate beneficial ownership per the Companies Act 1993 and the AML/CFT Act 2009 where the company is considered a reporting entity; file a reporting entity summary with the Companies Office if any shares are held by a trust or corporate nominee.
required_dossiers: New Zealand Register of Directors particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late-filing penalty may be imposed (currently NZD 3.00 per day up to NZD 300.00); remedy by immediate e-filing and request for waiver through the Companies Office penalty remission process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Department Registration – IRD Number, GST, and PAYE
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand – online myIR portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a New Zealand income tax number (IRD number) via the online IRD registration form (IR596 or digital equivalent) indicating the business activity as 'Non-destructive testing, commercial inspection and certification services' (ANZSIC 7120). Assess GST registration requirement; mandatory if annual turnover exceeds NZD 60,000, and voluntary registration is available (with input credit benefits) for taxable exporter services; register for GST on a payments basis or quarterly filing basis as appropriate. If hiring local staff, register for PAYE and employer superannuation contribution (KiwiSaver) scheme.
required_dossiers: Shareholder and director ID, tax numbers
Bank account details of New Zealand trading account
GST registration election and business activity statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD requests further substantiation of non-resident director authority, provide a resolution of the board and certified extract of the incorporation register; penalties for late GST/PAYE filing are curable by voluntary disclosure under the Tax Administration Act 1994 s. 138H to reduce shortfall penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Bank Account and Enabling Cross-Border Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand-registered trading bank (e.g., ANZ Bank New Zealand Limited, ASB Bank Limited, Bank of New Zealand, or Westpac New Zealand Limited); Financial Markets Authority (FMA)-authorized reporting entity for AML/CFT compliance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate NZD currency account and ancillary foreign currency (USD and EUR) accounts for the receipt of wire-transfer payments and disbursements via Wise. Provide certified formation dossiers, beneficial ownership declaration, and business plan substantiating the independent factory inspection and lab testing agency. Complete the bank's client due diligence (CDD) using the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) and documentation evidencing that the directors have AEOI/CRS status and the company is not a shell entity without substance. Execute banking resolutions and e-banking mandates.
required_dossiers: Director ID verification and in-person/bank officer interview
Resolution of the board authorizing bank account opening and payment rail subscriptions
Register of significant controllers or beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application due to beneficial ownership complexity, restructure direct shareholding to eliminate nominee layers, provide a New Zealand substance attestation with office lease and employment records, or apply to an alternative authorised bank. If an AML/CFT assessment is adverse, submit a supplementary compliance plan to the bank's AML/CFT compliance officer and await FMA guidance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Corporate Governance Framework and First Board Resolution Formalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the company (under Companies Act 1993); Companies Office for any change to constitution registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a first board meeting with due notice to all directors. Adopt the board minutes and the pro-forma first board resolution covering share allotment, registered office address, service of address, director appointments, authorization of banking relationships, and designation of the company's annual reporting entity classification under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 (small / look-through / exempt company status). Resolve on the delegation of authority to the managing director/chief executive officer for the solicitation of inspection clients and the procurement of professional indemnity insurance.
required_dossiers: Notice of Meeting of the Board
Draft minutes of the First Board Meeting
Constitution (or deemed constitution rules under s. 16)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director disagrees, record a formal dissent and proceed by majority vote subject to the constatation of quorum; if any resolution violates the Companies Act 1993, cure by supplementary resolution and disclose at the next annual shareholders' meeting.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: WorkSafe New Zealand (the Crown entity responsible for workplace health and safety), together with the New Zealand Accreditation Service (NZAS) under the International Accreditation New Zealand (IANZ); for certain manufactured-product inspection, Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) or Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) may impose additional technical accreditation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Workplace Operator Licence / Accreditation under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 and the Testing and Inspection Accreditation ('Fit-for-Purpose Quality Control Service Permit') issued by IANZ for conformance with ISO/IEC 17020 (inspection bodies), where applicable to factory pre-shipment inspection services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) of New Zealand
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration Level / Permitted Activity (not requiring a full EIA Report), classified under the Resource Management Act 1991 s. 88A and Schedule 4 as a low-impact commercial laboratory and mobile inspection service; general non-notified status unless the factory testing facility includes significant liquid waste discharge or hazardous chemical storage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance thresholds: wastewater discharges to sewer or land must meet the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards) Regulations and local city/district plan standards (e.g., pH 6.0–9.0, BOD5 < 300 mg/L, suspended solids < 400 mg/L for discharged trade waste as set by the local council); VOC emissions from any solvent-based cleaning or calibration operations must not exceed 100 mg/Nm3 (or 0.5 kg VOC per batch) as tested per Australian/New Zealand Standard AS/NZS 3580; hazardous waste (industrial test chemicals, metals, and used calibration gases) must be managed under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008, using an authorized waste contractor, with manifesting and disposal consents from the territorial authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (Form FS 51) from Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) confirming compliance with the Fire Safety and Evacuation of Buildings Regulations 2006 for any permanent office, calibration laboratory, or sampling facility of more than 50 people or covered by an evacuation scheme; structural load clearance and building warrant of fitness (BWoF) from the local territorial authority for occupied premises; WorkSafe New Zealand occupational health and safety clearance, including health and safety policy, supervision plan, hazard register, risk assessment under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, and a worker participation system; certification of first aid and emergency response supplies, and if vehicles are used for on-site factory inspections, compliance with the Land Transport Act 1998 for light and heavy motor vehicles.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Taake), Wellington, New Zealand — principal online portal 'myIR' (https://www.ird.govt.nz); business registration coordinated via the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) registry (https://www.nzbn.govt.nz) and the New Zealand Companies Office (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate a New Zealand International Company (IC) with the NZ Companies Office or, if a foreign-incorporated entity, register as an overseas company; obtain the NZBN as the common Master Data identifier. Step 2 — Apply for an IRD number (New Zealand tax file number) through myIR using the non-resident company application form (IR596) or via the myIR business account; the IRD number serves as the statutory TIN for income tax and GST purposes. Step 3 — Register for GST using the GST registration form (GST101A or online via myIR) if annual taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000, or voluntarily where a refund position is expected; non-residents supplying 'remote services' to NZ consumers must register under the GST (Cross-border) rules regardless of turnover. Step 4 — Where applicable, file an election for 'Exempt Foreign Company' status (form IR453) with the IRD within the statutory deadline (generally by the first two income years) to maintain a tax-exempt offshore profile. Step 5 — Register as an employer (IRD employer number) only if hiring NZ-based staff; otherwise no PAYE obligations arise. Step 6 — Open a NZ or offshore bank account and notify the IRD of the appointed New Zealand agent for service of notices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — The CK International Company (CK_IC) is treated as a New Zealand foreign company that, if it elects and continues to qualify under section EX 21B of the Income Tax Act 2007, is an 'Exempt Foreign Company' (EFC): all shareholders are non-resident, the company is not controlled from New Zealand, it derives no New Zealand-sourced income, and it carries on no business in New Zealand. As an EFC, the entity is wholly outside the New Zealand income tax net, effective as a statutory tax-exempt offshore zone, while remaining a limited liability legal person. Absent a valid EFC election, the default rule is that a company incorporated in New Zealand is tax-resident and therefore taxed on its worldwide income ('Entity_Level_Taxation' would then apply); however, for the CK_IC structure the intended and achieved status is Tax_Exempt_Zone via the EFC regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not have a 'check-the-box' regime. The relevant statutory elections for the CK_IC are: (i) Exempt Foreign Company election under sections EX 21A–EX 21B, Income Tax Act 2007 (filed on IR453), allowing a non-resident-owned IC to be treated as tax-exempt on non-New Zealand income; (ii) Hybrid and branch mismatch elections under Part FM of the Income Tax Act 2007 (introduced under BEPS), including the hybrid financial instrument exclusion and the surrogate branch election, to neutralise mismatches in double-tax relief; (iii) GST grouping election under section 55 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, if the IC is part of a GST group with NZ-resident members; (iv) Voluntary GST registration under section 51(3) of the GST Act, permitting the IC to register for GST even below the NZD 60,000 threshold to zero-rate export supplies and recover input tax; and (v) GST taxable-period elections (1-month, 2-month, or 6-month filing cycles) aligned with the anticipated refund profile.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — a comprehensive value-added tax governed by the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (GSTA 1985), administered by the Inland Revenue Department, with registration and filing conducted exclusively through the myIR digital channel.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 (compulsory registration once annual taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period, or reasonably expected to exceed in the next 12 months, per section 51 GSTA 1985). Voluntary registration permitted from the first dollar of taxable supplies (section 51(3)). Non-resident suppliers of 'remote services' (electronically supplied services, telecommunication services, and offshore services received by NZ-resident consumers as defined in section 8B GSTA 1985) are subject to a distinct statutory registration obligation with no de-minimis threshold, using the 'sole supply' rule for offshore-to-offshore business-to-business supplies to avoid double registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, no digital stamping, and no continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate. E-invoicing is voluntary and is implemented under the Peppol framework (NZ e-Invoice standard, adopted by the Digital Business Council); the IRD does not operate an API-based real-time clearance gateway for individual invoices. GST returns are filed electronically via myIR on a 1-month, 2-month, or 6-month cycle, with payment and filing required by the 28th day of the following month (or the 7th day of the following month for interest/penalty purposes on deferred payment). The myIR portal supports bulk electronic filing (EDIFACT/XML) but does not pre-validate individual invoices for VAT purposes; instead, IRD conducts risk-based post-return audit mining of invoice-level data. The practical effect for the CK_IC is that paper/PDF invoices remain fully valid, but a Peppol-conformant e-invoicing protocol is recommended for audit transparency and to support the zero-rating evidence trail.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The CK_IC may zero-rate its supplies of on-site factory pre-shipment inspection, testing, and quality-control services under one of two mutually exclusive limbs of the GSTA 1985: (1) Goods — where the inspection/testing itself is incidental to the supply of exported tangible goods, zero-rating applies under section 11(1)(a) provided the goods are physically exported by the supplier or on the supplier's behalf within the statutory timeframe (in practice, within 12 months or as evidenced by the Customs export entry). (2) Services — where the CK_IC supplies services to a non-resident client who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, and the services are performed wholly or predominantly outside New Zealand, the supply is zero-rated under sections 11(1)(b) and 11(1)(c) (the 'offshore services' rule). For on-site factory inspection performed at an offshore factory (e.g., a manufacturing plant in the People's Republic of China), where the CK_IC contracts with a non-resident principal (e.g., an overseas importer, foreign government agency, or supranational buyer), and the inspection report is delivered to the non-resident client offshore, the supply qualifies for zero-rating provided none of the section 11(1)(c) exceptions apply (i.e., the services are not directly in connection with land in New Zealand, not directly in connection with goods in New Zealand, and not supplied to an individual physically present in New Zealand). Where the CK_IC's NZ trading entity performs inspection on NZ soil for goods to be exported, zero-rating may nonetheless be available under section 11(1)(b) if the recipient is a non-resident and the services relate to goods being exported by the recipient; the IRD applies the 'directly in connection with goods' test strictly. The CK_IC must maintain contemporaneous documentation proving the non-resident status of the counterparty (e.g., certificate of incorporation, tax residence certificate, and bank details), the physical location of the factory, and the offshore delivery of the report.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: NZ Customs Service Export Declaration (Trade Single Window entry) — evidencing the outward movement of the goods, including the Customs Unique Identifier and the declared export value
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill — showing the consignor as the CK_IC or its agent, the consignee as the offshore customer, and the destination port/airport outside New Zealand
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Transaction Record — bank proof of receipt of the export settlement in NZD or convertible foreign currency, referencing the relevant export invoice

Executed inspection and testing services contract — identifying the non-resident client, the offshore factory premises, the scope of the pre-shipment quality-control work, and the delivery terms of the inspection report

Detailed inspection report and photographic evidence — including GPS-stamped factory coordinates, date-stamped photos of the tested goods, batch/serial numbers, and the certifying inspector's credentials

Certificate of Origin and/or Supplier's Declarations — where the goods are commodities subject to preferential origin rules, supporting the physical flow from the offshore factory to the importing jurisdiction

Invoicing pack — zero-rated GST invoice (clearly marked '0% GST — Exported Services' or '0% GST — Export of Goods'), together with all purchase orders, correspondence, and the foreign buyer's tax identification number (TIN/VAT ID)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Inland Revenue Department applies heightened audit scrutiny to zero-rated export claims by offshore-focussed entities such as the CK_IC, particularly where (i) the supplier cannot demonstrate physical export of goods or offshore performance of services, (ii) the counterparty is a related party or a zero-tax jurisdiction resident, (iii) the consideration is not repatriated within 180 days of the invoice date, or (iv) the documentation bundle is missing any mandatory component. Where the IRD determines that zero-rating was applied incorrectly or the substantive conditions were never met, it will issue a default GST assessment converting the supply to the standard rate (15%), raising the net GST liability retrospectively from the tax period in which the supply was originally returned, and charging use-of-money interest (presently 9.53% per annum under the IRD prescribed rate on underpayments) from the original due date. In addition, the Tax Administration Act 1994 imposes tiered shortfall penalties: 20% of the resulting tax shortfall for failing to take reasonable care; 40% for gross carelessness; 100% for an 'abusive tax position' (i.e., a position taken with a dominant purpose of avoiding tax that is not reasonably arguable); and 150% for evasion or an arrangement with the dominant purpose of defeating the intent of the GST Act. Where the CK_IC, its directors, or its agents knowingly submit false or misleading export zero-rating claims, the IRD may prosecute criminally under section 143A TAA 1994 (maximum imprisonment of 5 years and/or fine of NZD 50,000 for individuals, with an additional automatic penalty equal to the unpaid tax), and under section 143B the corporate entity is liable to a fine not exceeding NZD 100,000. The IRD also has power under Part 9 TAA 1994 to issue a 'tax avoidance arrangement' determination, striking down the purported export structure and any associated GST refund, together with a 100% shortfall penalty for an abusive tax position where the arrangement is void as against the IRD. Furthermore, where the 180-day FX repatriation deadline is missed without a demonstrable commercial cause (e.g., documentary credit delay, bank error, or contractual milestone linked to the final acceptance certificate), the IRD can recharacterise the transaction as a domestic supply, regardless of the underlying export evidence, and claw back the zero-rated status for the entire transaction. All refunds of input tax arising from zero-rated export positions are separately subject to an IRD 'integrity check' before release, and the commissioner may withhold a refund pending completion of a full records inspection under section 46 TAA 1994.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. New Zealand abolished formal exchange controls in 1984, and there are no legal restrictions, approvals, or licensing requirements imposed by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand on the conversion of NZD into foreign currency or on the repatriation of dividends, capital, or service fees. The Financial Markets Authority (FMA) separately regulates financial market conduct. Profit remittance is subject exclusively to tax compliance obligations (e.g., Non-Resident Withholding Tax on distributions if applicable), not to currency control authorization. For an exempt International Company with substantive inspection and testing operations in New Zealand, no overseas investment consent is required for ordinary cross-border service remittances; however, if a non-resident acquires significant land or sensitive business assets in NZ, the Overseas Investment Act 2013 consent regime could apply, which is not triggered by routine banking or FX activity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation, or mandatory conversion requirements on export proceeds. An exporter of on-site factory pre-shipment inspection, testing, and quality control services may retain, invest, hedge, or disburse foreign currency receipts offshore without any obligation to convert them into NZD within a specified timeline. Banks will nevertheless apply standard anti-money laundering transaction monitoring and may request supporting contracts and invoices to evidence the commercial substance of each inbound transfer.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (New Zealand) Limited (ANZ Bank New Zealand)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility with regulatory caveats. Wise (formerly TransferWise), Airwallex (NZ), OFX, and Convera are registered as Financial Service Providers on the New Zealand Financial Service Providers Register (FSP) and are subject to the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act 2009) as reporting entities. Wise is expressly targeted in the payment rails and remains the preferred fintech channel because it offers multi-currency settlement, local NZD bank account details, and pragmatic KYC documentation for cross-border service businesses. However, a fintech EMI cannot solely substitute for a Tier 1 commercial bank requirement: the entity's status as a tax-exempt International Company will be reviewed as a higher-risk customer by EMIs, requiring the same underlying economic-substance evidence and beneficial ownership disclosure. Full functionality (SWIFT outbound, commercial LC capacity) is unavailable via fintech EMIs; they are viable only for operational funding and operational disbursements, not for escrow or trade finance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical in-person KYC interview is effectively mandatory for an International Company with non-resident ownership applying for a corporate bank account in New Zealand. Under the AML/CFT Act 2009 and the regulations and codes of practice issued by the Department of Internal Affairs, no bank may open a corporate account without completing customer due diligence on directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners. Most Tier 1 New Zealand banks require at least one director or the authorised principal to attend a face-to-face interview at a branch in New Zealand; remote and video-based electronic identity verification is permitted in theory, but in practice banks almost always require a physical meeting or a certified verification conducted by a New Zealand-registered solicitor or qualified accountant for tax-exempt international entities. The entity must maintain a registered office in New Zealand and be registered on the New Zealand Companies Office register with current directors and address details. A fully remote account opening without a prior banking relationship is not practically available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt International Company status classified as a tax haven or high-risk zone flag during bank on-boarding and CDD/EDD review
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full economic-substance package: executed client inspection/testing agreements with Asian agrifood importers, on-site factory audit contracts, comprehensive business plan, staffing payroll records, office lease, local licence or certification (e.g., ISO 17020 or export inspection licences), profit-and-loss projections, and a written legal opinion from a New Zealand-qualified tax counsel confirming the exempt status derives from NZ specific legislation and not from a no-tax jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed or partially identified ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) residing outside New Zealand, triggering ownership-chain red flags and correspondent-bank restrictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO chain to the final natural persons: certified passports or national identity cards, proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement not older than 3 months), each shareholder's and director's curriculum vitae and business biography, a trust deed where applicable, a register of significant controllers filed with the NZ Companies Office, and statutory declarations of source of wealth and source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk industry-class mismatch between invoicing description (inspection/testing) and expected payment flows from procurement-heavy overseas clients that may resemble trade-based money laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed service agreements with clear fee schedules, purchase orders, pre-shipment inspection reports and certificates of conformity issued per shipment, supporting photos and audit trails, exact-match contract-to-invoice amounts, invoices with accurate ISIC-based service descriptions, and independent confirmation from the counterparty bank that its client is a legitimate manufacturer or importer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to evidence the commercial rationale for a tax-exempt structure combined with rapid cross-border wire volumes, triggering SAR filing by the reporting entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group structure chart, intercompany service contracts with arm's length pricing, operational substance in New Zealand (staff, premises, insurances), correspondence from a recognised New Zealand corporate services provider, historical settlement track record with verifiable audit trail, and quarterly reconciliation of inspection revenue against time sheets and factory visits.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: New Zealand has no mandatory purpose-code regime for wire transfers; payment instructions are processed via SWIFT MT103 (ISO 20022 in the NZD local clearing context) with BBAN/IBAN-style account references. For optimal reconciliation, the remitter should populate the wire reference with the ISIC-coded service description (e.g., 'FACTORY INSPECTION QC SERVICES', Contract/PO number) and the transaction narrative should state 'Trade-related business services under ISIC 7120'. The beneficial owner's name, the beneficiary bank branch SWIFT code, and the NZ account number in the format used by the local exchange settlement (e.g., ANZ/NZ bank prefix, branch and account fields) must be accurate. Inbound FX conversions from USD, EUR, CNY to NZD should be executed through the receiving bank's spot desk or Wise's mid-market conversion; no Reserve Bank approval is required. For share capital injection, the corporate law identifier in the payment narrative must reference the board resolution; capital is freely credited to the operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For fee payments to overseas subcontractors, laboratories, and auditors, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 via the transmitting NZ bank's correspondent network (typically via Australian or US correspondent banks for USD, EU banks for EUR, and Chinese RMB via CNH clearing in Hong Kong). For payment of NZD-denominated invoices within New Zealand, the clearing rail is the Reserve Bank-owned Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) used by the immediate payment system and the Settlement Before Interchange (SBI) network. For any trade settlement where the inspection/testing agency acts as an intermediary purchasing goods for resale (not standard for ISIC 7120), a commercial Letter of Credit (LC) may be arranged through the issuing bank with SWIFT MT700/MT707 messages; however, for the core fee-for-service model, MT103 electronic transfers and Wise's automated wholesale settlement are sufficient. Outbound transfers require upholding screening against NZ sanctions lists and the bank's internal AML risk appetite.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Spot Contracts (same-day or T+2 settlement in NZD)
Outright FX Forwards (standard deliverable forwards up to 12 months, freely permitted and tradeable in the NZD market)
FX Swaps (swap of principal at inception and reversal at maturity, used for liquidity funding)
Currency Options (European-style vanilla call/put options for asymmetric risk protection)
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS/CRS licensed by the FMA and permitted under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 where prudential requirements are met)

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible in New Zealand but are economically unnecessary because NZD is freely deliverable; regulators prefer deliverable instruments to avoid any question of speculative positioning; NDFs may only be offered by a registered derivatives issuer under the FMC Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act 1993, s 208) — confirmation of registered office, directors, shareholders, and beneficial ownership particulars.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation & Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the anniversary of incorporation (the company's annual return date).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty (approx. USD 30–65 per return); continuing default may subject officers to personal penalties and lead to administrative deregistration/strike-off of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Statutory Audit Report (mandatory only for 'large' companies, FMC reporting entities, and issuers).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Directors and, where filing is required, the New Zealand Companies Office / Registrar of Companies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Board approval and issuance within 5–6 months of the balance date; delivery to the Companies Office within the same statutory window for companies required to file.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Officer fines up to NZD 10,000 (approx. USD 6,000) for failure to prepare, approve, or file financial statements; continued non-compliance may trigger deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (IR4) — annual return of assessable income, deductions, and imputation credit account details.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 7 July following the balance date for a standard 31 March balance date; extension of time arrangements permitted.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 (first year) or NZD 500 (subsequent years); late payment usage-of-money interest (UOMI); possible prosecution for repeat/defaulted filers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accreditation / Regulatory Licence Renewal for commercial inspection, testing, and quality-control certification services (ISIC 7120).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: International Accreditation New Zealand (IANZ) / Ministry of Business, Innovation & Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of the accreditation/licence issue date; renewal application due no later than 30 days before expiry.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Lapse of accreditation invalidates legally recognised pre-shipment inspection/testing reports; MBIE may issue cease-and-desist directions and clients may reject issued test certificates.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is mandatory for FMC reporting entities, issuers, and 'large' for-profit companies where total assets exceed NZD 60 million or total revenue exceeds NZD 30 million in each of the two most recent consecutive financial years. Small and medium companies below these thresholds, with no public accountability, are exempt from statutory audit unless shareholders resolve otherwise.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Equivalent IFRS (NZ IFRS) for Tier 1 entities; NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime for Tier 2 entities; NZ Small & Medium Entity Accounting Standard (NZ SME) for Tier 3 entities; tax-basis simplified reporting permitted for certain small exempt entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Directors must maintain a beneficial ownership register and confirm its accuracy during each annual return filing with the Companies Office. The confirmation must identify every significant person holding or controlling 25% or more of shares or control rights, and record all share-transfer or beneficial ownership changes occurring during the year. Failure to maintain or correctly confirm the beneficial ownership register is a statutory offence.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800–4,800 per annum for a small-to-medium entity statutory audit; USD 600–1,200 for financial statement compilation only

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying International Company (CK_IC) in the tax-exempt zone: 0% New Zealand income tax on foreign-sourced income if the company is not a New Zealand tax resident and has no New Zealand permanent establishment. New Zealand-sourced business income derived by an IC through a branch or agency is taxable at 28%. No imputation credits are generated on exempt foreign income. The domestic statutory corporate rate for a New Zealand-resident company is 28%; losses carried forward are subject to the schema limit of 5 years for this exempt-zone model, notwithstanding New Zealand domestic law's indefinite carry-forward rule subject to shareholder continuity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return, filed electronically through Inland Revenue myIR or approved EFTS/software gateway. Non-resident companies with New Zealand-source income use IR4 and must have a New Zealand IRD number.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Provisional tax is payable in three instalments during the income year for a standard 31 March balance date; the final IR4 return is completed once after year end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Standard 31 March balance date: IR4 due 7 July immediately following the tax year. Non-standard balance date: return due on the last day of the second month following balance date. Registered tax agents may obtain extension-of-time arrangements from Inland Revenue; terminal tax due date may be aligned with provisional tax filing in the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income before expenses, including gross inspection and QC service revenue, testing fees, commissions, interest, royalties, and any New Zealand-sourced assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident IC with no New Zealand PE: include only New Zealand-sourced income if any; exclude foreign-sourced exempt income; insert 0 if no New Zealand-source activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenses incurred in earning assessable income, including salaries, subcontracted inspectors, laboratory consumables, equipment leases, travel, insurance, and allocated administrative overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses incurred in deriving New Zealand-sourced income; allocate shared or group overheads on a consistent arm's-length basis and retain supporting documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss from business after expenses. Calculated as Box 1 minus Box 2.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an exempt IC with no New Zealand PE, report nil; do not mix exempt foreign income with the New Zealand branch calculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Losses carried forward or losses offset against current year assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only apply losses that arose from New Zealand-source assessable income and satisfy shareholder continuity rules; exempt-zone foreign losses are not available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying available loss offsets and any statutory deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an IC with no New Zealand-source income, taxable income is zero. Include only New Zealand branch taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax on taxable income at the company rate of 28%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not apply the 28% rate to exempt foreign income. If Box 5 is zero, insert 0 here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits claimed: resident withholding tax, imputation credits, provisional tax paid, foreign tax credits, and any treaty relief credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident IC may claim only credits properly creditable against New Zealand tax liability; attach supporting tax credit statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual tax payable by the company or refund due after applying all tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For nil filers, enter 0. If the statutory NRWT was over withheld, a formal refund claim may be filed with Inland Revenue within the applicable 4-year limitation period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: initial late filing penalty NZ$250, followed by NZ$50 for each month or part-month the return remains outstanding. Late payment: initial penalty of 1% of unpaid tax plus 1.5% per month thereafter, with use-of-money interest charged from the original due date. Unacceptable tax positions attract shortfall penalties of 20% or 40%, and intentional evasion attracts a 150% shortfall penalty. Continued non-filing can result in prosecution and a fine of up to NZ$50,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% domestic Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) on gross dividends paid by a New Zealand-resident company. Treaty relief generally reduces the rate to 15%, and to 5% for a corporate shareholder beneficially owning at least 10% of voting power under most New Zealand DTAs. For a non-resident exempt IC, distributions sourced outside New Zealand are outside NRWT; a distribution sourced from New Zealand could be caught at the domestic rate absent DTA relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide the New Zealand withholding agent with a valid Certificate of Residence (obtained from its home tax authority) and a declaration of beneficial ownership. The withholding agent then applies the relevant treaty rate and accounts for NRWT through the IRD payment schedule. The annual return reconciliation identifies treaty-rate dividends, interest, and royalties. Records must be retained for 7 years. If the statutory rate has been under-deducted or if refund is sought, the non-resident should file a New Zealand return or refund claim within the statutory 4-year period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: domestic NRWT 15%; treaty-reduced rates generally 10% under principal New Zealand DTAs, with some treaties at 5%. Royalties: domestic NRWT 15%; treaty-reduced rates generally between 5% and 15%. An Approved Issuer Levy of 2% may apply to interest paid by an approved New Zealand issuer in lieu of NRWT where the recipient is non-associated and the instrument meets statutory conditions. Payments characterised as technical service, management, or inspection know-how fees may be recharacterised as royalties if they involve intellectual property transfer or use.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZ$10 million annual aggregate cross-border related-party transactions triggers Inland Revenue's contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation expectation. Mandatory Country-by-Country reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of NZ$1.3 billion or more. Master File and Local File are not filed annually but must be produced within 30 days of Inland Revenue request in a transfer pricing risk review.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand tax law does not operate a separate economic substance filing regime for ordinary companies; corporate residence is determined by incorporation in New Zealand or where the company's head office, centre of management, or director control is in New Zealand. The General Anti-Avoidance Rule in section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007 may recharacterise arrangements that lack commercial substance and are undertaken for a tax avoidance purpose. For the tax-exempt IC, economic substance must be maintained in its home jurisdiction: physical office, resident directors, employees, core business decision-making, and appropriate books and records. If an IC is managed and controlled from New Zealand, it is treated as New Zealand tax resident, losing its exempt-zone status and becoming taxable on worldwide income at 28%.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating income from factory inspection and quality control services, fabricating supplier or subcontractor expenses, or falsely claiming non-resident exemption for income that is in substance New Zealand-sourced.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Shortfall penalty of 150% of the tax underpaid under section 141E of the Tax Administration Act 1994; criminal prosecution with fines up to NZ$50,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years; use-of-money interest and late payment penalties apply; assessment time bar extended indefinitely in cases of evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or direct the evasion are jointly and severally liable for the tax shortfall where the company is a façade; personal prosecution, director disqualification, asset restraint orders, and travel bans may be imposed by the court.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the CK_IC with no physical office, no employees, no board meetings, no substantive business activity, and no annual economic substance records, while management and strategic decisions are exercised from New Zealand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the IC as a New Zealand tax resident under the head-office and management control rules; worldwide income taxed at 28%; invalidation of the exempt-zone tax position under GAAR; shortfall penalties up to 150%; deregistration or strike-off by the Companies Office; cancellation of export or professional licences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can have the corporate veil pierced where the IC is used as a sham; they may be held personally liable for unpaid tax, ordered to make restitution, subjected to travel bans, and prosecuted criminally for fraudulent insolvency or tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging related-party overseas entities below-market inspection fees, paying inflated management fees to a tax-haven entity that performs no actual service, failing to prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for cross-border related-party dealings above NZ$10 million, or maintaining no benchmark study.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may make an arm's-length adjustment and reallocate assessable income; shortfall penalties of 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for a dominant position, and 150% for intentional evasion; use-of-money interest; CbC reporting penalties up to NZ$100,000 for non-compliance; director penalty notices may attach to unpaid corporate tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who are parties to artificial profit-shifting arrangements may be personally liable for shortfall penalties, subject to disqualification, restrained from leaving New Zealand by court order, and prosecuted for money laundering or tax fraud where proceeds are moved offshore.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing trust and company services for the IC without an AML/CFT compliance programme, failing to conduct customer due diligence, failing to report suspicious transactions, or accepting client funds from high-risk jurisdictions through wire transfer or digital payment rails without identification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 of up to NZ$2 million per breach for a body corporate; individual fines up to NZ$200,000; criminal money laundering offence under the Crimes Act 1961 punishable by up to 7 years imprisonment; asset forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly permit the movement of criminal proceeds face personal criminal liability, significant fines, confiscation orders, travel bans, and imprisonment; professional licences required for statutory inspection and QC activities may be revoked.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Treating dividends, royalties, or service fees as exempt foreign income while the true source is New Zealand, or using the IC as a conduit to strip profits from New Zealand operations without paying NRWT, imputation obligations, or applicable royalty withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Anti-avoidance reassessment imposing 28% corporate tax plus NRWT at 30% on deemed dividends or at 15% on deemed interest/royalties; penalties of 20%, 40%, or 150%; use-of-money interest; refund claims for treaty relief denied if the recipient lacks substantive ownership or beneficial entitlement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed false declarations or caused the repatriation structure to misstate its tax character can be held personally liable, face civil restitution, departure prohibition orders, and imprisonment for deliberate tax fraud.
